answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity to a costly, verifiable stake instead of free accounts: each agent locks a deposit in a shared harbor registry, and its reputation accrues only through attested work over time, like stars slowly condensing from a nebula rather than appearing overnight. A newcomer with a sable record of no history starts with near-zero trust and limited access, so spinning up thousands of fresh identities buys nothing — influence must be earned through sustained, costly, checkable contributions, and misbehavior burns the stake.
